column1: # xfrm_audit.tsv -- KNOWN data-plane defects, declared at their exact value.
# Every live row is audited by xfrm_audit.sh (ICV length, packet counters,
# per-SA integrity failures, /proc/net/xfrm_stat error counters).  A row
# listed here is XFAIL for that check; when the defect is fixed the audit
# reports XPASS and FAILS the row so the entry has to be deleted.
#          stat  (value: Counter=N[,Counter=N]  -- may rise by at most N)

column4: RFC 5685 two-gateway redirect row: the child's SAs are keyed to the LIVE sibling C but there is NO SPD policy row — spmd_pfkey.c refuses a tunnel-policy install when my_sa_ipaddr is absent ('No my_sa_ipaddr'), the same unpin that lets ike_determine_sa_endpoint follow the redirect.  Without an SPD row the harness's xa_probe never fires, so nothing moves data at row end by design.  The row's proof is the failover LANDING: initiator wire re-target to the LIVE sibling C + C and I both holding keyed ESP child SAs (esp>=2) while draining A stays at 0.  Data-plane traversal is explicitly out of scope for this landing row.
